question: A long piece of paper \(5\) cm wide is made into a roll for cash registers by wrapping it \(600\) times around a cardboard tube of diameter \(2\) cm, forming a roll \(10\) cm in diameter. Approximate the length of the paper in meters. (Pretend the paper forms \(600\) concentric circles with diameters evenly spaced from \(2\) cm to \(10\) cm.)
solution:
Under the stated model, a turn with diameter \(d\) centimeters contributes \(\pi d\) centimeters of paper. We therefore need the sum of the \(600\) circumferences.

Pair the smallest diameter with the largest, the next smallest with the next largest, and continue inward. Every pair has diameter sum \(2+10=12\) cm: moving inward increases one diameter and decreases the other by the same spacing. The \(600\) circles form \(300\) pairs, with each circle used once.

Each pair contributes \(12\pi\) cm of paper, so the total length is
\[
300(12\pi)=3600\pi\text{ cm}
=\boxed{36\pi\text{ m}},
\]
using \(100\) cm per meter. The approximate length is therefore \(36\pi\) meters, choice A.
